title: Retorsion: Rome's faithful cannot better tell true councils from false than our people tell canon from apocrypha
source_text: XIV. Et certe multi, quos Ecclesia Romana pro vere fidelibus habet, non magis possunt per se dignoscere germanum Ecclesiae suae testimonium a supposititio, verumque et legitimum Concilium ab illegitimo, et Canones veros ab adulterinis, quam fideles e plebe nostra particulam libri Canonici a particula Apocryphi. Atque etiam viri in ea Ecclesia docti de quorundam suorum Conciliorum authoritate disputant, nec satis inter se consentiunt an legitima sint an secus. Et tamen illi tuentur Ecclesiae suae doctrinam et testimonium esse supremam fidei regulam, cujus authoritas a nulla superiori authoritate pendet, et cui se fideles immediate subjicere debent, a Spiritu sancto moti atque impulsi.
pass_a_gloss: And certainly many whom the Roman Church holds for truly faithful can no more by themselves distinguish their Church's genuine testimony from a forged one, and a true and lawful Council from an unlawful one, and true Canons from adulterated ones, than the faithful from our common people can distinguish a particle of a Canonical book from a particle of an Apocryphal one. And even learned men in that Church dispute about the authority of some of their Councils, and do not sufficiently agree among themselves whether they are lawful or not. And yet they maintain that their Church's teaching and testimony is the supreme rule of faith, whose authority hangs on no superior authority, and to which the faithful ought to subject themselves immediately, moved and driven by the Holy Spirit.
pass_b_english: Plenty of people Rome itself counts as true believers are no better at spotting a forged church-testimony, an unlawful council, or adulterated canons than our ordinary hearers are at spotting Apocrypha next to Canon.
Even their own learned men quarrel over whether some councils bind, and they do not settle the question among themselves.
Still they insist their church's teaching and witness is faith's supreme rule, depending on no higher authority, and that the faithful must submit to it at once under the Spirit's impulse.
